key_insight: Rather than compressing or discarding visual tokens, VISOR saves compute by performing vision–language interactions only when and where they are needed, using sparse, dynamically selected cross-modal connections. This preserves fine-grained visual information while substantially lowering inference cost.
problem_solved: Reduces inference cost of Large Vision–Language Models without creating an information bottleneck from aggressive visual token reduction, which degrades performance on fine-grained and reasoning-heavy tasks.
method: Maintain dense visual representations but apply a lightweight selector/gating mechanism to decide which regions/visual tokens participate in cross-modal computation.
Trigger sparse, on-request vision–language interactions (conditional cross-attention or adapters) only for selected queries or regions, avoiding costly full cross-modal processing every step.
Integrate the selector with the LVLM pipeline to balance accuracy and compute, allowing dynamic adjustment per input and task.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy high-performing LVLMs with much lower inference cost, preserving fine-detail reasoning without sacrificing throughput — useful for real-time, resource-constrained, or large-scale multimodal deployments.

paper_title: VISion On Request: Enhanced VLLM efficiency with sparse, dynamically selected, vision-language interactions
paper_authors: Adrian Bulat, Alberto Baldrati, Ioannis Maniadis Metaxas, Yassine Ouali, Georgios Tzimiropoulos
